question: Do repository-local pipeline evidence, trajectory, and recovery artifacts create competing operational authorities or unbounded lifecycle state?
verified_evidence: 247 plans and 159 learnings are tracked; current operation adds 77 untracked plan files and 43 untracked learning files
plans/checkpoints contains 217 files, including 121 files under acceptance-runs; representative files are mutable task/session/runtime evidence keyed by external IDs
29 of 202 learning files have under 100 non-heading characters; representative auto-extracted files contain empty What happened and What to do sections
repository code, scripts, and docs have no consumer references to plans/checkpoints, plans/tasks, or learnings roots
commit 2a4a68ea339 preserved a large mixed batch of product changes and pipeline artifacts before upstream sync, coupling external run history to product commits
31 repository-local trajectory pointer files exist (29 untracked, 2 tracked), none of their referenced runtime JSONL targets exists, and neither pointer nor target pattern is ignored
the npm package files allowlist excludes these roots, so they are not required distribution content
conclusion_so_far: Verified: pipeline evidence and extracted learnings form an unbounded second history inside the product repository; trajectory pointers are incomplete runtime residue and a false session-state surface. Recommended boundary is canonical external task/KM storage for run evidence, curated durable docs only in product Git, and runtime trajectory state outside the checkout.
next_trace: None; report completed. If discussed later, identify the external canonical retention location and migration policy before deleting historical artifacts.
